To: Marius Momeu <marius.momeu@berkeley.edu>
Subject: libgit2-crustify: api.c's export gateway justifies its parser handles by more than C promises

Hi Marius,

This is an incorrect safety justification, not a reachable defect, so it can be handled in
public.

In \`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs\` (commit b3d6b9b37), the gateway under
\`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c\` builds each export's parser handle with \`parser_mut\`, whose
\`// SAFETY:\` comment says the parser's \`settings\` and \`data\` meet \`set_settings_ptr\`'s and
\`set_data\`'s contracts, "which is what C's own callers of \`llhttp_execute\` promise". Those
contracts now ask that the table's callbacks be sound at any time while the parser holds it.
libgit2's HTTP client does not keep that: it leaves its static table installed and sets
\`data\` to NULL between calls (\`transports/httpclient.c:1283\`, \`1473\`, \`1529\`, \`1565\`),
and its callbacks dereference \`data\` unconditionally (\`httpclient.c:163\`).

The exports are sound all the same, since each handle lives for its export's call alone,
during which C keeps its table and context. The fix rests the comment, and \`table()\`'s, on
that confinement; no code changes. It is on crustify/waves/wave-194, with the report under
\`crustify/reviews/modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/wave-194/batch-6/contracts/ffi_export/\`.

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` wave 194 batch 6: review of batches 1, 3 and 4's symbols

This batch reviews the `symbol` route of batch 1 (`2c69341c3`: `llhttp.c`'s `Parser::new`,
`reinit`, `parse`, `Callback`, `DataCallback` and the X-macro maps, a wrapper reviewed on its
public API) and api.c's whole `port`, batches 3 (`2a51ccb3f`) and 4 (`b3d6b9b37`), whose 31
exports serve C scheduled for porting and were reviewed for what that C relies on. Every
objective applies, `fix` included. It files four findings: two `+internal` (`contracts`), and
two `+misc`, a test that breaks the switch and the ownership store's missing records.

- **contracts** (`ffi_import`): `set_settings_ptr` and `set_data` bounded the table and the
  context by when the parser "executes", which batch 4's safe dispatchers make at any time. A
  caller who frees the table after its last parse reaches a heap use after free from safe
  code (`on_message_complete()`, ASan). Both now hold "for as long as the parser holds it",
  until a setter replaces it or `reinit` clears it, `reset` keeping it. The regression tests
  are two `ub_unsafe` tests that call the dispatchers outside any parse.
- **contracts** (`ffi_export`): `parser_mut`'s and `table()`'s justifications said C's callers
  meet those contracts. libgit2's HTTP client leaves its table installed with `data` NULL
  between calls, and its callbacks follow `data` unconditionally. The exports are sound because
  each handle lives for its call alone, and the comments now say so.
- **misc**: with the archive lacking `api.c.o` and the export feature on, `ub_unsafe` did not
  link. Batch 5's fixture `refuse_url` calls `llhttp_set_error_reason`, which has no export.
  Batch 4's link check had run before its rebase onto batch 5. The fixture now writes the field,
  as the C function's body does.
- **wavefront/ownership**: batch 4 submitted no pointer findings for its 28 functions that have
  pointers (`llhttp_finish`, `llhttp_reset`, the name functions and the dispatchers); they are
  now submitted. The dispatchers keep one pending slot per parameter, since wavefront merges
  `llhttp.c`'s prototype into api.c's signature
  (`crustify/evolution/wavefront-two-prototypes-one-signature`).

What held. `parse`'s two panics, on a parser with no state and on a callback that parses or
re-initialises the parser it is lent, are the right refusals: C aborts or corrupts its run, and
the trampolines' barrier turns the panic into the callback's error. The thread-local register
cannot be bypassed: the handles are neither `Send` nor `Clone`, a handler gets a handle and never
the `Parser`, and registrations nest. `HPE_PAUSED_H2_UPGRADE` leaves `_current` at `s_error`, so
clearing its error reaches the panic, not `abort`. Every other setter a callback may call
mid-parse changes only fields the generated code branches on. The dispatchers as safe public
methods are sound under the corrected contracts. Their cost is that a C table's callbacks must
be sound at any time while the parser holds them. libgit2's own C does not do that between
calls, so its Rust port must clear the table along with `data`, as the corrected `set_data` says.
Checking the 23 dispatcher exports against a transcribed `Dispatcher` type matches `llhttp.c`'s
prototypes (`llhttp.c:569–616`) and api.c's definitions in ABI. It checks only the batch's own
transcription, as `exports-without-a-header-declaration` says, and wavefront's merged records
above corroborate it. The 13 items ported onto `llhttp.rs`'s accessors behave as api.c's
one-line bodies do, and `port-onto-an-existing-accessor`'s rule fits them. A C callback given
an empty span receives a dangling pointer, where C passes `p`. That is a pointer's value, which
no C consumer here reads. The proposal `obligation-spans-what-the-holder-keeps` records that
this module's two contract findings share one cause.

Tests: 2 `ub_unsafe`, passing on plain and ASan+UBSan. Run alone under Miri, each stops at
`llhttp_init` (`calls C`). BSan was not run, since nothing here is expected to trigger it. The
module's tests pass on plain (`lib` 6, `equiv` 25, `ub_safe` 22, `ub_unsafe` 17, `unit_pub` 72,
doctests 16 and 9) and under ASan+UBSan. With the export feature on, over scratch copies of
gen1's `plain` and `asan-ubsan` archives lacking `api.c.o` (211 objects), `lib` 860 (1 ignored),
`ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 137, `unit_pub` 156 and `hidden_symbols` pass. Under ASan,
`ub_safe`'s known `compile_fail` mismatch is the exception. `nm` shows the 31 exports defined and
api.c's others absent. `equiv` is excluded by design. Coverage: `run.sh` on this tree, read with
`report.py` from the scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and
`unit_pub`. The pp cells are against batch 4's figures for this base. `ub_unsafe`'s Rust moves
`+0.46` pp; the other deltas are noise, since those suites did not change. Worklist: `api.rs`
187 of 187 lines, 39 of 39 functions and 226 of 227 regions. `llhttp.rs` has 291 of 310 lines,
76 of 77 functions and 338 of 362 regions, the misses batch 1's compile-time helpers, its
`pub(crate)` C constructors and trampoline refusals, which a wrapper gets no tests of. The
gateway is compiled out. The safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as batch 4's) differs
from batch 4's recorded scan of the base only in test counters (`code.tests.loc.total` `+54`,
which the Overview takes). `ffimap api` against the base (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's
private rustdoc JSON): the 65 anchored keys are `kept`, the two private macro ports `missing`,
and every unattributed module `kept`.

Gates, on the base `b3d6b9b37`, the wave branch's tip: `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes
with warnings denied with the export feature off and on, and the changed files are formatted
with nightly rustfmt. Usage cells are the assistant's.

content.text:
I reviewed the three landings, filed and fixed four findings, and landed two commits on `crustify/waves/wave-194` (`083e7a467` with the reports, `2f0cf4265` with the fixes). The wave branch hadn't moved since my base `b3d6b9b37`, so the rebase under the landing lock was a no-op. No gate needed rerunning after it, because nothing new came in to combine with.

## Findings, all fixed
- **Contract (`ParserMut::set_settings_ptr`, `ParserMut::set_data`):** both said the table and its context must stay valid "while the parser executes". Batch 4's dispatchers are safe methods that can run at any time, so that wording isn't enough. My reproducer keeps the table alive for the parse, frees it, then calls `on_message_complete()` from safe code, and ASan reports a heap use after free. Both contracts now say "for as long as the parser holds it", until a setter replaces it or `reinit` clears it (`reset` keeps it). Two new `ub_unsafe` tests call the dispatchers outside any parse.
- **Export justification (`parser_mut`, `table()`):** the comments claimed C's callers meet those widened contracts. libgit2's `httpclient.c` doesn't: it leaves its table installed with `data` set to NULL between calls. The exports are still sound because each handle lives only for its own call, and the comments now rest on that. No code changed.
- **Switch-breaking test:** with `api.c.o` removed from the archive and the export feature on, `ub_unsafe` failed to link. Batch 5's test fixture `refuse_url` calls `llhttp_set_error_reason`, which has no export. Batch 4's link check ran before it was rebased onto batch 5, so it missed this. The fixture now writes the `reason` field directly, as the C function does.
- **Wavefront records:** batch 4 submitted no pointer findings for its 28 functions that take or return pointers; I submitted them.

## Verdicts on the four points you asked about
- **`parse`'s panics** (a parser with no state, and a callback that parses or re-initialises its own parser) are the right refusals. I couldn't get around the per-thread registry: a handler only ever gets a handle, which can't be sent or cloned. The H2-upgrade pause leaves the parser at `s_error`, so clearing it reaches the panic, not `abort`.
- **Safe public dispatchers** are sound under the corrected contracts. The cost is that a C table's callbacks must be safe to call at any time while the parser holds them. libgit2's own C doesn't keep that between calls, so its Rust port will need to clear the table along with `data`.
- **Dispatcher exports checked against a hand-copied type:** it matches `llhttp.c`'s prototypes and api.c's definitions, but it only checks the batch's own transcription, as the `exports-without-a-header-declaration` proposal says.
- **The 13 items ported onto `llhttp.rs`'s existing accessors** behave like api.c's one-line bodies, and the `port-onto-an-existing-accessor` proposal's rule fits them.

## Gates and measurements
- **Clippy:** passes with warnings denied, export feature off and on. The changed files are rustfmt-clean.
- **Module tests:** pass on plain and ASan+UBSan.
- **Link check** (scratch copies of the plain and ASan archives without `api.c.o`, 211 objects, feature on): `lib`, `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `unit_pub` and `hidden_symbols` pass. Under ASan the one exception is `ub_safe`'s known `compile_fail` snapshot mismatch. `nm` shows all 31 exports defined. `equiv` is excluded by design, since it calls api.c's C.
- **Miri:** the two new tests stop at `llhttp_init` ("calls C"), as their markers say.
- **BSan:** not run; nothing here is expected to trigger it.
- **Coverage:** measured on this tree. `api.rs` is now 187 of 187 lines.
- **ffimap:** changes only in test counters.
- **API diff:** all 65 anchored items `kept`.

## Evolution
- **Proposed:** `wavefront-two-prototypes-one-signature`. wavefront merges api.c's definition and `llhttp.c`'s own prototype into a six-parameter record, so the dispatchers' records can never be complete.
- **Proposed:** `obligation-spans-what-the-holder-keeps`. Batch 5's finding and mine have the same cause: an obligation timed by calls that safe code can still make later.
- No spec change was made and no lesson recorded. Usage cells are left to you.

I deleted my scratch builds from `crustify/tmp/` and the worktree's `target/`.
